Notebook: Resendiz: 'Being hunted instead of the hunter' is different
Makes first 168 defense vs. Munguia on Saturday; Zayas-Ennis undercard set; Zuffa's 1st U.K. card: Billam-Smith vs. Rozicki; Azim fight set; new Queensberry show announced; Quick hits; Show & tell
A note to Fight Freaks Unite readers: I created Fight Freaks Unite in January 2021 and eight months later it also became available for paid subscriptions for additional content — and as a way to help keep this newsletter going and for readers to support independent journalism. If you haven’t upgraded to a paid subscription please consider it. If you have already, I truly appreciate it! Also, consider a gift subscription for the Fight Freak in your life.
Armando Resendiz was the hunter when he last fought last May as an unknown underdog. Now he holds the WBA super middleweight title and is the hunted.
In that last fight, Resendiz challenged former IBF super middleweight titlist and heavy favorite Caleb Plant, who was supposed to breeze to a defense of his WBA interim belt and set up a fight with former middleweight titlist Jermall Charlo, who had done his part by winning the co-feature.
But a funny thing happened on the way to the expected Plant win. Resendiz, who found out a few days before the fight that he was going to become a father for the first time with a son on the way, was intensely motivated by the news.
He was far from the soft touch many expected as he took control of Plant in the second half of their fight with relentless pressure and won a well-deserved split decision and the interim title in the 2025 Fight Freaks Unite upset of the year.
In December, Resendiz was elevated to full titleholder when undisputed champion Terence Crawford retired and now heads into his first defense against Mexican countryman and longtime contender Jaime Munguia aiming to show that the win over Plant was no fluke.
They will fight in the David Benavidez-Gilberto “Zurdo” Ramirez co-feature on the PBC on Prime Video Cinco de Mayo weekend pay-per-view card on Saturday (Prime Video PPV and DAZN PPV, 8 p.m. ET) at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas.
